templates_considered: audit_log_protected (RET-001): fit for the audit table write restriction
no_destructive_sql (SEC-010): did not fit; no raw SQL in the ask
retained_data_cleaned_up / retained_data_has_age_limit (RET-002/003): did not fit; ask is about tracking changes and runaway loops, not retention
endpoints_need_login / own_records_only: did not fit; not about access control
no_sensitive_data_in_logs (LOG-001): did not fit; not about logging content
reads_are_paged (PERF-001): considered for cost; does not target AI spend or loops
middleware_surfaces_errors, external_calls_handle_errors: considered for retries; not the unbounded loop problem

rules.covers: only the audit function writes the audit log
every table holding a customer email is tagged
objects reaching email tables record the change
AI calls never run inside loops
no unbounded while loop, so no forever-retry

ask_parts_not_covered.part: AI call cost of $900 in a loop (total spend)
background task retrying forever (retry count and frequency)
ask_parts_not_covered.why: no check exists; task retries not checkable. Covered only by removing while loops and writing a bound by hand

ask_parts_not_covered.part: who changed what on email tables: every write actually goes through the audit
ask_parts_not_covered.why: couldn't tell how; object.statement_required only checks the call exists, not that writes in triggers or direct SQL are audited

ask_parts_not_covered.part: whether audit rows are reviewed or retained

assumptions: customer-email tag name is free to choose and is not in any vocabulary
orgs.billing_email counts as a customer email
retry cap of 5 attempts is acceptable to the customer
deleting nightly_ticket_summaries is acceptable; the customer approved the plan but summarising tickets nightly is gone
users table holds customer-facing emails too, so it is tagged
confusions: Table tag syntax (tags = [...] at table level) was not in the skill or the workspace files; placed after auth and the dry run accepted it, but I did not confirm it is the correct location.

Skill is very long (about 110KB of output) and the check catalogue has no per-check examples for statement.containment placement names; I guessed must_not_be_inside with foreach/for/while from the example.
Recipes do not cover audit trails for write changes; I used RET-001 plus a hand-written object.statement_required rule.
Deleting a task file: the dry run did not show the deletion, and I could not tell whether push deletes without --force.
object.statement_required placement param is listed in the catalogue but its doc said 'unconditional' meaning top level; I assumed it applies to functions called by the object too.
wished_for: A recipe or template for 'audit who changed what on tables holding a class of data' that names the write-restriction and per-writer call pattern.
A check or param that bounds AI spend or flags AI calls in loops across called functions, or a spend-cap check.
Clear statement of whether deletions of objects appear in a dry-run preview and need --force.
Examples of table-level tags syntax in XanoScript.
dry_run_problems_seen: nightly_ticket_summaries deletion not shown in dry-run preview
why_confidence: AI-in-loop and while-loop rules are real checks and will report, but spend and retry counts are not checkable; the audit rule only confirms a call exists in each writer and the existing writers are not yet updated, so AUDIT-010 will report findings until they are. Policies unevaluated.
